payload.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

ambiguities: It is not stated whether the coefficients are meant to be nonnegative integers or merely nonnegative numbers, though the standard interpretation is nonnegative integers.

The phrase if the quotient is a polynomial in q leaves open whether the polynomial is taken after cancellation in a rational expression or in some other formal sense, though the standard reading is the formal polynomial obtained by simplification.
The quantifiers over n, k, and l are simultaneous in effect, but the wording could be read as one universal quantifier over triples.
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The Gaussian q-binomial coefficient is used in its standard definition.
The coefficients of the relevant polynomial are intended in the usual expansion in powers of q.
The condition on q as an indeterminate is implicit rather than quantified.
The inequalities force n to be nonnegative even though the statement says integers n, k, l.

domain_restrictions: n, k, and l are integers
the quotient is only assumed to have meaning as a polynomial when it simplifies to one in q
the phrase has only nonnegative coefficients refers to the standard expansion as a polynomial in q
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer triple n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the ratio of the Gaussian binomial coefficient for n choose k to the one for n choose l is actually a polynomial in q, then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: for every integer k satisfying 0 <= k <= n
for every integer l satisfying 0 <= l <= n
if the quotient of the two Gaussian binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q, then its coefficients are all nonnegative
